environment_audit.docker_status: Docker CLI (v29.2.1) is installed, but the Docker Desktop Linux Engine daemon (//./pipe/dockerDesktopLinuxEngine) was not active because Docker Desktop requires interactive GUI startup/EULA acceptance and com.docker.service requires Administrator elevation. Therefore, Kafka containers were not running locally.
environment_audit.throughput_non_monotonic_root_cause: The previous in-process benchmark enforced target emission rates using Python's time.sleep(target_duration - elapsed). On Windows, the default system timer resolution is 15.625 ms (64 ticks/sec). For target rates like 25,000 rows/s with micro-batches of 500 rows, target_duration is 20 ms. Calling time.sleep() for ~15 ms frequently caused the Windows thread scheduler to suspend the process for 2 timer ticks (~31.25 ms), artificially collapsing throughput down to 24-38 rows/s. At 100,000 rows/s, target_duration was 5 ms (< elapsed), so time.sleep was completely bypassed, allowing unthrottled execution at 7,000+ rows/s. This timer quantization created the severe non-monotonic throughput artifact.
